subject: ventures/link-keeper
professional: a marketing-operations / web-analytics lead who runs campaign link tracking (and answers to a data-protection officer); first checks: does every short link land on exactly the URL it was given, with UTM tags per the Google Analytics campaign-URL convention and the existing query untouched; are bots and link-preview fetchers kept out of click counts; do iPhone, iPad and Android visitors reach the right store; and is the 'no IP stored' privacy story true of what sits on disk

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with `node /tmp/claude-0/audit-linkkeeper/probe.mjs` and `node /tmp/claude-0/audit-linkkeeper/srv.mjs` against the Google Analytics campaign-URL convention (utm_source/medium/campaign appended to the existing query, fragment kept) and RFC 3986 section 3.4/6.2.2 (the query is opaque; normalisation must not decode or encode reserved characters). Right: https://example.com/pricing?ref=x#top -> ...?ref=x&utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=oct-launch#top; an existing utm_source=old is replaced in place; hand count of 3 desktop clicks from 2 visitors plus 1 curl bot on day 1 and 1 repeat visitor on day 2 gives clicks 4, bots 1, uniqueVisitorDays 3, and the engine agrees; a 2026-11-01..2026-11-17 stats window has 17 days (inclusive); maxClicks 1 gives 302 then 410; CSV neutralises '-2+3', '@cmd' and tab-prefixed cells per OWASP CSV-injection guidance. Wrong: the browser planner splits each line on every comma, so a destination with a comma in its query (https://example.com/search?ids=1,2) silently becomes the link https://example.com/search?ids=1&utm_... with short name '2': a wrong destination, no error. addUtm rewrites the whole query through URLSearchParams even when no tag is given: ?q=a%20b&flag -> ?q=a+b&flag= and ?a=1;b=2 -> ?a=1%3Bb%3D2, which changes meaning for servers that treat ';' as a separator or test for a valueless flag. An iPadOS 13+ Safari UA (desktop-class 'Macintosh' string, Apple's default since 2019) is classified macos/desktop, so iPad visitors get the web URL, not the iOS target.
evidence.completeness: Every README API route works end to end (probed in srv.mjs and covered by server.test.mjs): create with slug/utm/ios/android/expiresAt/maxClicks/tags, bulk up to 200 with per-item results, list with tag and q filters, get, PATCH, DELETE-archives-to-410 and PATCH {archived:false} restores, stats with from/to, CSV export, '/:slug+' preview, HEAD does not count, ALLOW_HOSTS, ROOT_REDIRECT, REDIRECT_STATUS, hourly prune at 400 days, batched saves with flush on SIGTERM. Planner on index.html plans and copies the bulk body. Gaps: README lists PATCH {utm?} but utm without url is silently ignored (PATCH {utm:{source:'x'}} returned 200 with the URL unchanged); PATCH cannot change ios/android targets or tags; the preview page shows only the default URL. Malformed input gives 500 instead of 400: GET /%E0 (URIError), bulk {links:[null]}, PATCH body 'null'. No stubs or TODOs. Served copy rewrites llms.txt (source points at the old github.io address) to marisstella.app (`node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs link-keeper`: no placeholder or retired origin left).
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/link-keeper && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 33 tests, 33 pass, ~0.35 s (engine 11, server 8, page 5, usage 9). Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: click-limit >= -> > caught; bots counted as clicks caught; prune window +30 days caught; android routed to the ios target caught; credential check reduced to password only SURVIVED (the only credential test URL has both user and password); iPad tablet classification removed SURVIVED. No test covers a comma in a pasted URL, query preservation on tagging, an iPadOS UA, or salt deletion. A failing server test hangs the runner: assertions sit before srv.close() with no t.after/finally, so the first mutant ran until killed (about 4 minutes, under the tool's 900 s timeout); mutations were rerun with --test-force-exit.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (197 lines), server.mjs (124), index.html script, engine.test.mjs, server.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs. Zero dependencies, pure engine shared by browser and server, timing-safe bearer compare, escaped HTML, CSP and no-referrer on server pages, atomic write via rename, body size cap, strict slug regex, case-insensitive slug keys. Defects: decodeURIComponent on the public path and JSON bodies that are not objects throw TypeError/URIError and fall through to 500 plus a stack in the log; dense one-line handlers (server.mjs:44-77) are hard to review; cfg.save() writes the whole state synchronously on every create/PATCH; server tests leave the server open on failure.
evidence.claims: Backed: one process with a JSON file (server.mjs), zero dependencies, only http(s), no credentials, reserved slugs, referrer host only (refHost), no raw UA or IP in state (server.test.mjs:115), bots apart and not consuming maxClicks, 400-day retention, 302 default and the 301 caching note, disclaimer on README and page footer, local-only opt-out usage counts with DNT/GPC (usage.test.mjs). Not backed: README:81 and the page FAQ say the unique-visitor salt 'is discarded at the end of each UTC day'; it is replaced only at the first non-bot click of a later day (engine.mjs:141) and is written to the state file with that day's HMAC(ip|ua) keys, so after a quiet period the salt and hashes sit on disk for weeks, and anyone with the file can test a known IP+UA against them. 'Any link can be inspected without being followed by adding a plus sign' (index.html:75): the preview shows link.url only, while an iPhone visitor is sent to the ios target (srv.mjs: preview showed https://example.com/web, iPhone got https://evil.example.net/x). 'Existing utm_* values ... are replaced, other query parameters are kept' (index.html:54): kept but re-encoded. Planner label 'optionally followed by a comma and the short name' does not warn that commas inside URLs break the line.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a small SaaS marketer deploys the server, plans a newsletter's links in the page, posts the bulk body, sends the links and reads stats a week later. That works for ordinary URLs: tagged destinations, short names, app-store routing for iPhone and Android, expiry, per-day clicks, referrer host, device and CSV. In the first hour they would hit: a filtered product URL with a comma lands on the wrong page with a nonsense short name; iPad visitors get the web URL; stats are JSON only (stated); PATCH utm alone does nothing. Stated limits (no dashboard, no QR, no teams, JSON file) are honest and fit the indie buyer.
evidence.domain: Compared with the Google Analytics campaign-URL convention (utm_source/medium/campaign/term/content; GA4 also reads utm_id, utm_source_platform, utm_creative_format, utm_marketing_tactic, not supported), RFC 9110 15.4 redirect semantics (302 default, 301/308 cached; right), RFC 3986 query opacity (departs: full re-serialisation), Apple's iPadOS desktop-class UA (departs: iPads miss app routing), and the daily-salt unique-visitor method used by privacy-first analytics such as Plausible, whose documentation says salts are deleted after 24 hours (departs: salt kept until the next click on a later day, stored beside the hashes). Bot filtering is a hand regex rather than the IAB/ABC spiders and bots list; Googlebot, Twitterbot, Slackbot, facebookexternalhit and curl are caught. Sources cited from my own knowledge, not fetched.

defects.what: The campaign planner splits each pasted line on every comma or tab, so a destination with a comma in its query (https://example.com/search?ids=1,2) silently becomes a link to https://example.com/search?ids=1&utm_... with short name '2', and the 'Copy bulk API body' button carries that wrong destination to the server. A redirect to the wrong destination is the product's own first kill criterion.

Privacy claim overstated: the unique-visitor salt is not discarded at the end of the UTC day; it is replaced only at the first click of a later day and is persisted in the state file next to that day's HMAC(ip|ua) keys, so after a quiet spell the salt and hashes stay on disk indefinitely and a known IP+UA can be tested against them.
The '+' preview, sold as the way recipients check a link before opening it, shows only link.url; iPhone and Android visitors are sent to targets.ios / targets.android, which the preview never shows.

addUtm re-serialises the whole query through URLSearchParams, even with no tags: ?q=a%20b&flag becomes ?q=a+b&flag= and ?a=1;b=2 becomes ?a=1%3Bb%3D2, changing the destination for servers that read ';' separators or valueless flags (RFC 3986 treats the query as opaque).

iPadOS 13+ Safari sends a desktop-class 'Macintosh' UA by default, so iPad visitors are classed macos/desktop and get the web URL instead of the App Store target; no iPad heuristic or note in the README.
README lists PATCH {utm?}, but utm without url is ignored and the call returns 200 with the URL unchanged; PATCH also cannot change ios/android targets or tags.
Malformed input returns 500 with a logged stack instead of 400: a bad percent-escape on the public path (GET /%E0, URIError from decodeURIComponent), bulk {links:[null]}, and a PATCH body of 'null'.

Server tests call srv.close() after their assertions with no t.after/finally, so any failing server test leaves the listener open and the suite hangs instead of going red (a seeded mutant ran about 4 minutes until killed).
Two seeded mutants survive: the credential check reduced to password-only (no test URL has a username without a password) and iPad tablet classification.

verdict: A tidy, honest, zero-dependency shortener whose server API does what the README lists: create, bulk, archive to 410, expiry and click limits, bots kept out of counts, per-day stats that recompute exactly by hand (4 clicks, 1 bot, 3 visitor-days), OWASP-style CSV neutralisation, and a page with the disclaimer and local-only usage counts; 33 tests pass and 4 of 6 seeded mutants are caught. It misses the bar on correctness and claims. The browser planner, the page's front door, splits pasted URLs on every comma, so ?ids=1,2 becomes a link to ?ids=1 named '2' without an error, which is the product's own kill criterion (wrong destination). Tagging re-encodes the existing query (flag -> flag=, ';' escaped). iPads get the web URL. The privacy line says the visitor salt is discarded daily, but it sits in the state file beside the hashes until the next click on a later day, and the '+' safety preview hides the device-specific destinations. Failing server tests hang rather than fail.
